title: Movie title years and metadata tails
summary: Replaced global movie token deletion with title preservation plus verified metadata-tail cleaning in Python and PowerShell. Release years now use bracketed precedence or the rightmost plausible 1888-through-next-year candidate while preserving earlier title numbers; packaged numeric remove defaults are migrated safely.
reason: Global category regexes and leftmost-year selection could corrupt legitimate names such as 12 Angry Men, 10 Cloverfield Lane, DC League of Super-Pets, 2001 A Space Odyssey, 1917, 1984, and Blade Runner 2049.
behavior_before: Ambiguous words such as Web, Cam, DC, Ma, Audio, and Proper could be deleted anywhere; the first year-like number could become the release year; the legacy packaged remove list globally removed 01-12; empty cleaning could reintroduce raw release metadata.
behavior_after: Authoritative title text is preserved, ambiguous terms clean only within verified release metadata tails, PROPER/REPACK/RERIP clean only as revision tails, only the selected year occurrence is removed, exact legacy defaults normalize in memory and persist on the next confirmed Settings save, and metadata-only names block preview or use the production Unknown Movie fallback.
manual_validation: Bundled Python unittest: 129 movie, preview, config-contract, settings-store, settings-patch, app-config, and config-validation tests passed.
Real Python-to-PowerShell naming-preview differential passed for 19 numeric-title, plausible-year, ambiguous-word, and revision-tail filenames.
Invoke-NamingSupportChecks.ps1 passed with packaged-default, custom-list, metadata-tail, title-preservation, and safe-fallback coverage.
Invoke-ReleasePackagePolicyChecks.ps1 passed with dry-run package evidence.
rollback_plan: Revert the Python and PowerShell movie-cleaning helpers, packaged defaults, compatibility normalization, destination fallback, and their tests together. Existing customized remove lists remain data-authoritative and require no rollback migration.
notes:
Packet 3 protects numeric and metadata-like movie title text while constraining aggressive cleaning to verified release tails.
Refreshed generated summaries for all Packet 3 source and test changes.
No representative real-media validation is required because this packet changes filename/config planning only and uses disposable preview/config fixtures without FFmpeg, publish, scratch, or source-media processing.
